newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat must stay competitive for exports - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat must stay competitive for exports - HGCA.

text.p: UK wheat exports will have to remain strong in the second half of the season (July-June) to prevent a large build-up in stocks, the Home Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Wednesday.

In its latest supply and demand update, the HGCA said trade estimates put wheat shipments to end-December at between 2-2.5 million tonnes against a forecast export availability of about 4.5 million tonnes.
This meant that with no direct support for feed wheat, UK wheat prices would have to adjust to maintain the competitive position of exports.
The Ministry of Agriculture (MAFF) put barley export availability for this season at just under 2.3 million tonnes.

Trade estimates put shipments to end-December at over one million which made it unlikely for shipments to take up all the surplus barley this season with large amounts expected to be offered into intervention, the HGCA said. So far offers totalled only 2,500 tonnes.
In the first three months to end-September grain usage by human and industrial processors was 2.38 million tonnes -- a rise of two percent on the same period a year before.

Wheat consumtion was up three percent to 1.52 million while the usage of barley by maltsters and distillers rose by one percent to 495,000 tonnes. Malsters' use was likely to stay close to the high level seen last season of two million tonnes.
Wheat used by animal feed processors rose four percent to 686,000 tonnes while barley increased by 27 percent to 285,000.
Wheat stocks held on-farm at the end of September totalled 11.55 million tonnes, 16 percent higher than the previous season. Barley totalled 3.07 million tonnes, up 25 percent.
